issues.what: Reported: the Lado cells go to British Africa because belgian-congo/ledger/1 names british-africa, before the Sudan's 1910 gain. Checked: in the compile the Sudan's own gain (anglo-egyptian-sudan/ledger/4, 10 June 1910) takes 101 Lado cells from belgian-congo and the Congo's loss finds nothing, so 1910-1913 is right (Central Equatoria 183 cells Sudan in 1910, 1912).

Same land, 1914 onward: the Sudan's ledger/6 (1 January 1914, exchange with Uganda) is written over the whole 'Lado Enclave' region, so all 109 northern Lado cells went to british-africa in 1914 (trial without my event: british-africa in 1914 and 1915, back with the Sudan only in 1916 through the keyframe of 1916). The page dates the southern half to Uganda in 1912 and an exchange of an unspecified 'part of the enclave' on 1 January 1914; the land that went to Uganda 'was renamed West Nile'. Event gives back the part inside modern South Sudan (109 cells), the outline the dossier's own 1912 and 1916 keyframes use. The page does not say which cells the 1914 exchange moved (confidence 2).

Reported: the Mosul occupation by british-colonial-empire (14 November 1918) stays open at the 1920 anchor and should close in 1926. Since the report the p1910-p1919 reviewer changed events/2 from occupation_start to gain (with keyframe_overrides/1), so there is no open occupation: in the trial Mosul (333 cells of the five governorates) is british-colonial-empire 1918-1921, occupied by british-colonial-empire in the mandate hatch from August 1921, contested with the Republic of Turkey 1923-1925 (kingdom-of-iraq/ledger/3, 4 February 1923, the Mosul question left out of the Lausanne talks), and direct Iraq from 1926 (ledger/4, League award of 16 December 1925, Turkey assents in 1926). Only one cell of kingdom-of-iraq stays occupied by british-colonial-empire. The Mosul Question page says Britain occupied Mosul on 10 November 1918 (the Mesopotamian campaign page cited by events/2 says 14 November); the month is the same, so events/2 is left as it is.

Left over from the Mosul contest: when the contest ends in 1926 the Mosul cells (325) become plain direct Iraq, while the rest of Iraq (1,315 cells) stays hatched as occupied by british-colonial-empire until the mandate row ends in 1932. The pages opened (Mosul Question; British Mandate of Mesopotamia: 'to cover Ottoman Iraq', 'On paper, the mandate lasted from 1920 to 1932') do not say that Mosul was administered under the mandate after the 1926 settlement, so I did not add an occupation_start.

Darfur: the draft kept all of Darfur (1,811 cells) with british-africa from the 1916 conquest to the end of 1929. Cause 1: anglo-egyptian-sudan_1916 did not resolve ('Sarra Triangle'); the dossier now resolves (fx-45 disc, dossier edited 3 Nov 00:21), so no keyframe override of mine was needed. Cause 2, still there after the fix: british-africa/ledger/35 and the sultanate's own dissolution (6 November 1916, counterpart british-africa) moved the cells in 1916 and outrank the Sudan's keyframe snap of the same year, so Darfur stayed british-africa. Event gives it to the Sudan in 1917 ('The kingdom was incorporated into the Anglo-Egyptian Condominium in 1917'). Trial: Darfur 1,811 cells british-africa at the end of 1916, Sudan from 1917 to 1919 and in the p1920 anchor.

Italian Libya therefore has no 1912 gain, no 1912 keyframe and no 1915 retreat in the draft. dossier_requests.why: packet p1910-p1919, 'Unresolved regions (3)'. I did not patch them: they are not among my items and a patch event cannot replace the dossier's own ledger rows.

problems: Sarra disc is an exclave: the disc of dossier fx-45 (centre 21.83E 21.68N, 107 km) is drawn as a separate hexagon about 2 degrees west of the Sudan's outline in the 1917 image; the Libya-Sudan border page calls the Sarra Triangle 'the north-west corner of the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan' and gives the 22nd parallel (1925 treaty) and the 1934 border lines (25E south from Jebel Uweinat for 223 km, 20N west for 105 km, 24E south for 56 km) but no vertices. I wrote no polygon override, so as not to contradict the dossier.
p1930-p1939.json events/0 (Darfur to the Sudan from 1930) is now redundant: Darfur is already the Sudan's from 1917 (it finds no british-africa cells to take; harmless).

SE Libya is a larger fault outside my items: in the published draft british-africa holds about 1,940 Libyan cells from 1911 to 1929 (Cliopatria's British Africa shape) and about 1,880 are nobody's in 1914-1919; the p1920-p1929 Kufra ruling covers only the Kufra district.
The 1912 loss row of the Sudan (ledger/5, Lado southern half, counterpart uganda-protectorate) leaves 3 Lado cells to nobody in 1912-1914; negligible, not patched.
